summary: This is an excerpt from a first-person fiction narrative in which the narrator describes systematically sabotaging three mean girls at school: Rebecca, Lyndsay and Harper. The narrator plants stolen hair around Rebecca and in her hairbrush to make her think she is losing her hair, leaves chocolate truffles for Lyndsay, who has a self-destructive reaction to them, and sets Harper up with a fake romance that ends in disappointment. The narrator treats the revenge as deserved and satisfying, and the excerpt ends mid-scene at Harper's failed date.
one_line: A first-person fiction excerpt in which a narrator takes revenge on three cruel schoolgirls through hair pranks, poisoned treats and a staged romance.
key_facts: The narrator describes Rebecca as beautiful and smart, with perfect timing for making mean jokes.
The narrator collected hair matching Rebecca's hair color from the trash behind a hair salon.
The narrator slipped Rebecca's hairbrush out of her purse and jammed hair into it.
The narrator sprinkled hair on the floor by Rebecca's locker every day for a week.
Rebecca started skipping school, and her Facebook timeline filled with hair-related trauma.
The narrator left chocolate truffles all over the place for Lyndsay, who would eat them and then hate herself.
According to later hearsay, Lyndsay had to enter a residential treatment program for eating disorders.
Harper fell hard for a university student she had met at a party.
The university student sent Harper Tweets that were funny and sweet and made her feel special.
The student invited Harper on a special date to hear an amazing band.
Harper spent a fortune on pre-torn jeans and three new pairs of shoes for the date.
When Harper arrived at the date, the venue was not a bar but a poetry reading.
At the poetry reading, the cute guy was present but acted as if he did not know Harper.
